newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends lower on spec long liquidation.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends lower on spec long liquidation.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures ended sharply lower in light trading on Monday, pressured by speculative liquidation amid a perception of amble near-term supply, dealers said.

"Currently there is plenty of cocoa around and most manufacturers are covered through the summer," said Refco Inc analyst Ann Prendergast. "There's very little pressure for manufacturers to buy -- and it's keeping this market flat." July cocoa fell $20 a tonne on the day, to close at $1,449, after ranging from $1,467 to $1,445. Second-month September ended $16 lower, at $1,485, while the back months slumped $13 to $16.

Cocoa prices weakened at the outset, as speculators followed through on Friday's sell-off, traders said. Downward momentum picked up after the July contract triggered light sell-stops in the mid-$1,450s.
But July's failure to breach key chart support at $1,444 -- a low reached last week -- prompted locals to cover short positions, helping to lift prices off lows, traders said.
Some traders said the market could remain under pressure in the next two weeks as operators liquidate or roll over July contracts ahead of July's first notice day on June 17.
Technically, after $1,444, traders pegged July's next support level near $1,425. Near-term resistance was seen at today's high of $1,467.
